name: 39083-random2k-26b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of an a3 node (--gres=gpu:1).
architecture: Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration, bf16, ~51.6 GB on disk, apache-2.0, ungated; all shapes are in the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=16, bound = 160 requests + safety_seconds 1800, warmup 20%, no cooldown; about 144 requests fall inside the measured window, and the count is approximate because the boundary is a wall clock.
workload: 160 requests of random synthetic text, 2048 prompt tokens in and 512 output tokens out, both fixed rather than sampled; the output length is exact because the backend sets max_tokens and ignore_eos. Prompts are independently random, so there is no shared prefix. `backend.request_format: plain` is raw text completion with no chat template, and the prompt seed is static (39083).
purpose: A long-context text completion service on a 26-billion-parameter model, serving sixteen concurrent streams from one GPU.
launch:
model: google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it
tensor-parallel-size: 1
attention-backend: TRITON_ATTN
enable-prefix-caching: false
# 4096 rather than the checkpoint's own 262144-token window: the workload's worst case is
# 2048 + 512 tokens, so the cap is never binding. It bounds sequence length and gates a
# feasibility check; it does not size the KV block pool, which follows gpu-memory-utilization
# and free memory.
max-model-len: 4096
